name: Observation of high-energy neutrinos from the Galactic plane

significance.quote: We identify neutrino emission from the Galactic plane at the 4.5$\sigma$ level of significance, by comparing diffuse emission models to a background-only hypothesis.

summary.plain: Using machine learning on ten years of data, IceCube identified neutrino emission from the plane of our own Milky Way at the 4.5σ level of significance. The signal is consistent with modelled diffuse emission from the Galactic plane, but could also arise from a population of unresolved point sources.
summary.technical: Machine-learning cascade selection applied to ten years of IceCube data identifies diffuse Galactic-plane neutrino emission at 4.5σ against a background-only hypothesis; consistent with modelled diffuse emission but also compatible with unresolved point sources.

title: Observation of high-energy neutrinos from the Galactic plane
why_it_matters: The abstract says cosmic rays from the Milky Way arrive at Earth from random directions because of deflection in interstellar magnetic fields, but near their sources and during propagation they interact with matter and produce high-energy neutrinos; the paper searches for that neutrino emission from the Galactic plane.
